# Phase 9 gate report: resolving the 99% bar with a larger paired prompt set

**Status: complete. The gate deliverables are done (tests, experiment, this report, commit).**

Phase 8 left the study's headline in an awkward state. Brief §B8 asks for the minimum GPU KV budget
at which a policy retains at least 99% of full-cache NIAH accuracy, and at 45 prompts the query-aware
rungs landed within a fraction of one prompt of that bar at every context, on alternating sides. That
is a statement about the sample, not about the policy. The only way to turn it into one about the
policy is more paired prompts, so this phase ran
300 of them at
32,768 tokens, against Phase 8's
45.

## Gate checklist (CLAUDE.md rule 3)

- [x] **Tests run.** `pytest`, all passing. New: `tests/test_bar_resolution.py` pins the paired
  bootstrap (concordant prompts must add no width), the three-way rule at its boundaries, the
  prompts-to-resolve estimate (an effect on the bar must never resolve), and the chunk merge (a
  prompt counted twice, or chunks from different commits, are refused). §5 describes a race the
  suite caught during this phase, and the test that now makes it deterministic.
- [x] **Real experiment run.** `scripts/02_policy_quality.py --config configs/phase9.yaml`, in four
  chunks of 75 prompts via the new `--sample-start`, launched detached from a worktree pinned at the
  commit under test.
- [x] **Phase doc written.** This file.
- [x] **Committed and pushed.**

## What was measured, and the rule fixed before the run

| Axis | Setting | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Context | 32,768 tokens | The headline is defined at 32K. Phase 8 already showed the budget fraction travels across context; this phase is about the noise floor, not the axis. |
| Policy | Rung 5 (Quest-style) | Rung 6 is rung 5's selection over a CPU tier and was bit-identical to it in every cell of Phases 4-8, so its quality half would be a second copy of this measurement. |
| Budgets | 75% · 50% | The two that straddle the bar at 45 prompts. 25% and below miss it by more than sampling error at this N could explain. |
| Prompts | 300 per condition (20 per needle kind × depth) | Samples 0-2 are Phase 8's 45 prompts exactly (a prompt is keyed by its sample index), so the first chunk doubles as a reproducibility check. |

`configs/phase9.yaml` states the decision rule, and it was committed before the run started.
Retention is `sum(policy score) / sum(full score)` over the same prompts, and its 95% CI is a
percentile bootstrap that resamples *prompts*, so a prompt's two scores move together:

- **meets** the bar if the CI's lower bound is at least 99%;
- **fails** it if the CI's upper bound is below 99%;
- **unresolved** otherwise, reported as such.

Pairing is what makes this tractable at all. A prompt that both conditions pass, or both fail, adds
no width; the interval is made of the discordant prompts alone.

## 1. The verdicts

| Policy | Budget | Prompts | Retention | 95% CI (paired) | Verdict | Worse / better than full | Sign test p | Prompts to resolve |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 75% | 300 | 99.0% | 97.6–100.2% | **unresolved** | 12 / 6 | 0.24 | ~580,000,000 |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 50% | 300 | 96.9% | 94.7–98.9% | **fails** | 23 / 10 | 0.035 | ~300 |
| Block pool, 100% | 100% | 300 | 100.0% | 100.0–100.0% | **meets** | 0 / 0 | 1 | n/a (no discordant prompts) |

**The 50% budget fails the bar.** Its retention is
96.9%, with a 95% CI of
94.7%–98.9%:
the whole interval sits below 99%. It loses
23 prompts to the full cache and wins
10 back (sign test p =
0.035). At Phase 8's 45 prompts, the same rule
called it unresolved.

**The 75% budget is unresolved, and on this evidence more prompts would not resolve it.** Its retention is
99.0%, which is the bar itself, with a CI of
97.6%–100.2%.
Its margin over the bar is
+0.00 prompts out of
300. The observed discordance and effect put the
prompt count needed to separate it from the bar at
582,349,656, which is the delta method's way
of saying that the estimate sits on the bar. That is not a failure of this experiment.
It is the answer: the true retention at 75% is close enough to 99% that "does it clear 99%" is not a
question NIAH can settle on this machine, and the defensible statement is the interval.

The 100% block-pool control retains exactly what the full cache does on every prompt, so none of the
losses above come from the block layout itself.

## 2. What more prompts bought, prefix by prefix

The same rule at every prefix of the prompt set. The prefixes are the chunk boundaries, fixed by

| Quest-style (rung 5) | 75% | 45 (Phase 8's set) | 98.8% | 92.3–103.9% | 11.6 pp | -0.10 | unresolved |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 75% | 75 | 98.9% | 95.1–101.9% | 6.8 pp | -0.06 | unresolved |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 75% | 150 | 98.9% | 96.9–100.6% | 3.7 pp | -0.13 | unresolved |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 75% | 225 | 98.7% | 96.9–100.1% | 3.2 pp | -0.69 | unresolved |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 75% | 300 | 99.0% | 97.6–100.2% | 2.5 pp | +0.00 | unresolved |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 50% | 45 (Phase 8's set) | 95.0% | 86.8–101.9% | 15.0 pp | -1.60 | unresolved |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 50% | 75 | 94.5% | 88.8–99.3% | 10.4 pp | -3.06 | unresolved |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 50% | 150 | 95.4% | 91.6–98.7% | 7.1 pp | -4.88 | fails |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 50% | 225 | 96.5% | 93.7–98.9% | 5.2 pp | -5.19 | fails |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 50% | 300 | 96.9% | 94.7–98.9% | 4.2 pp | -5.75 | fails |

The two budgets behave differently as N grows, and the difference is the finding. At 50% the
interval narrows around a retention that stays several points below the bar, so it resolves once it
is narrow enough, and it stays resolved. At 75% the interval narrows around the bar itself: the
point estimate moves by a fraction of a point, never leaves the interval, and ends on the bar.
Six times the prompts shrank its CI width from
11.6 pp to
2.5 pp without moving it off the line.

| Policy | Budget | Needle kind | Prompts | Retention | Worse / better |

| Quest-style (rung 5) | 75% | multikey | 100 | 97.9% | 2 / 0 |

| Quest-style (rung 5) | 75% | single | 100 | 100.0% | 0 / 0 |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 50% | multikey | 100 | 93.6% | 6 / 0 |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 50% | multivalue | 100 | 98.2% | 16 / 10 |
| Quest-style (rung 5) | 50% | single | 100 | 99.0% | 1 / 0 |

Descriptive only; a third of the prompts cannot carry a verdict. The single-needle task is almost
never where rung 5 loses. The losses concentrate in the multi-needle kinds, which need several
distant blocks at once, so a selection that keeps most of them still drops a value. Multivalue is
also where rung 5 most often *beats* the full cache: those wins are partial-credit swings on
four-value answers, not evidence that approximation helps.

## 5. Erratum: the Phase 6 replay ablation raced, and its ceiling is optimistic

While this run was sharing the GPU, `test_replaying_a_recorded_selection_reproduces_the_run_exactly`
started failing most of the time. It was not the known kernel nondeterminism: pinning the
deterministic kernel made it fail every time, and recording the same pass twice stayed
bit-identical. The cause was a race in the tier (`lazykv/tiered.py`).

The gather-mode staging buffers are pinned host memory shared by every layer. Layer *L* fills them
and queues a non-blocking copy to the GPU; layer *L+1* fills them again. That is safe only if the
copy has run by then. In a real selection it always has, by accident: `rank()` moves the top-K
indices to the host, which syncs the stream at every layer. The replay ablation exists to remove
exactly that sync, so under load the host rewrote the buffers before the copy read them, and a step
attended to the wrong blocks. Disabling each guard in turn identified the staging buffers as the
culprit; the per-layer index buffer is guarded too, for the same reason.

The fix records a CUDA event after each copy and waits on it before the buffer is rewritten. On the
normal path the event has already completed, so the wait is free. A new test stalls the device with
`torch.cuda._sleep` so the host runs ahead every time; it fails without the fix and passes with it.

**What this does and does not affect:**

- Every quality result in Phases 4-9 is unaffected. Normal decode always synced, and rung 5, the only
  policy this phase measured, does not use the tier.
- **The Phase 6 ceiling is.** A correct replay must wait for the previous layer's copy before reusing
  the buffers, and the replay that produced the
  1.11–1.16×
  ceiling skipped that wait. The ceiling is therefore probably optimistic. Its replay token agreement of
  97.8%–99.3%,
  which Phase 6 attributed to kernel nondeterminism, was at least partly this race.
- Phase 6's conclusion, that taking the decision off the host is not worth a redesign, can only get
  stronger if the ceiling falls. But the number itself is not settled until it is re-measured, and
  that is a timing run that needs an idle machine. **Not measured yet.**

## 6. What this changes

- **Rung 5's minimum budget at 32K is not 50%.** That is now a measured failure rather than a noisy
  miss.
- **At 75%, rung 5 is indistinguishable from the bar,** and the indistinguishability is itself
  measured. The headline should quote rung 5's 75% retention with its interval, not a pass or a fail.
- **The 99% bar is too fine for NIAH at this scale** whenever a policy lands near it. A study that
  wants a pass/fail headline needs either a non-inferiority margin chosen in advance or a continuous
  metric (the teacher-forced KL is already measured for every condition).
